command: ffmpeg -nostdin -y -hide_banner -v error -fflags +bitexact -flags +bitexact -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=24:duration=6" -an -c:v libx264 -preset veryslow -crf 40 -pix_fmt yuv420p bars-16x9-24fps.mp4
why: 24 fps does not divide 60, so a composition at 30 fps ingests it through ffmpeg's resampler rather than frame-for-frame. testsrc2 moves in every region of the frame, so a tile that stops updating is visible in the picture rather than only in a hash.

command: ffmpeg -nostdin -y -hide_banner -v error -fflags +bitexact -flags +bitexact -f lavfi -i "testsrc=size=720x1280:rate=30:duration=6" -an -c:v libx264 -preset veryslow -crf 30 -pix_fmt yuv420p bars-9x16-30fps.mp4
why: Portrait against a landscape box: 9:16 drawn into 4:3 drifts 278 destination pixels, which is what `fit: "cover"` is declared for.

command: ffmpeg -nostdin -y -hide_banner -v error -fflags +bitexact -flags +bitexact -f lavfi -i "color=c=0x101820:size=1024x512:rate=30:duration=3[bg];color=c=0xf2c14e:size=192x192:rate=30:duration=3[fg];[bg][fg]overlay=x='(1024-192)*t/3':y=160" -an -c:v libx264 -preset veryslow -crf 30 -pix_fmt yuv420p wide-2x1-30fps.mp4
why: 2:1 against a 20:9 box drifts 80 destination pixels — over the one-pixel rounding floor and under a cover crop, so it is the clip `fit: "contain"` is declared for. A single moving box on flat colour is the smallest thing whose position states which source frame is on screen. The box moves by `overlay` and not by `drawbox`: on ffmpeg 8.0 a `drawbox` whose `x` is an expression rather than a literal draws nothing at all, silently, so the version above is not interchangeable with the obvious one.
